To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) we propose a general class of directed and weighted benchmarks for testing community detection algorithm; (b) we consider the possibility that a node belongs to multiple communities; (c) we apply the modularity optimization algorithm on our benchmarks and we compare the results with the ground truth.
We propose a general class of benchmark graphs for community detection algorithms that can be used to test directed and weighted networks.
we have proposed a new benchmark for community detection algorithms in directed and weighted graphs, with overlapping communities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of benchmark graphs to test community detection algorithms, with the aim of helping researchers to compare and to improve them.
the construction of a new benchmark for testing community detection methods on directed and weighted networks.
the generation of benchmarks with overlapping communities for directed and weighted graphs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, for the considered case of directed and weighted graphs, the modularity optimization algorithm performs well in the case of non-overlapping community structures, while it is not able to detect overlapping communities.
, while the modularity is a very good indicator of the presence of a community structure, it is not a good indicator of the number of communities in the network.

the benchmark graphs proposed here can be used to test and compare the performance of community detection algorithms, both on directed and undirected, weighted and unweighted graphs, with or without community overlap, in a controlled way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a benchmark that is flexible and can be adapted to the specific needs of the user.
we provide a general framework for testing community detection algorithm on a wide variety of networks with different features.
the proposed benchmark can be used for testing algorithms that are able to deal with directed and weighted graphs, and with overlapping community structure.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the community detection literature is now mature enough to allow for a systematic benchmarking of algorithms, which is a necessary prerequisite for a better comparison among different approaches.
the benchmark generation is a crucial step for the development of algorithms for community detection.
the benchmark graphs we propose are a useful tool to test the performance of community detection algorithms on a variety of complex networks with community structure.
